title: Children on DIC Awards: Age Limits and Dependency Reporting Terms
content:
Terms that govern children on a Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) surviving spouse award. Each term is the same in all six rate categories (DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate), DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) and DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision)).

## Schedule of terms

| Term | Setting (all six categories) |
|---|---|
| Child age limit — age at which a child stops being added to the spouse's award | 18 years |
| School-child age limit — age until which a school child may receive DIC in their own right | 23 years |
| Dependency report window — calendar days after a birth or adoption within which a report takes the event date as the effective date | 365 calendar days |
| Child permanently incapable of self-support before 18 | Stays on the award without an age limit |
| When a child addition ends (age) | The day before the child's 18th birthday |
| When a child addition starts on a timely report | The date of birth or adoption |
| Telephone report may remove a child or end the award | Yes |
| Telephone report may add a child | No |

## Questions this schedule answers

**At what age does a child stop counting on the spouse's award?** At the child age limit of 18 years; by age, the addition ends on the day before the child's 18th birthday.

**Is there any child to whom the age limit does not apply?** A child who became permanently incapable of self-support before 18 stays on the award without an age limit.

**What does the school-child age limit of 23 describe?** The age until which a school child may receive DIC in their own right. It is not an extension of the spouse's award.

**From what date does a child added on a timely report count?** From the date of birth or adoption, where the report reaches VA within 365 calendar days of that date.

**Can a telephone call change the children on the award?** A telephone report may remove a child or end the award; it may not add a child.

## Hypothetical dates

- A child born on April 9 is reported 365 calendar days after the birth: the report is inside the 365-day dependency report window and the addition starts on April 9. A report made on the 366th day is outside the window.
- A child whose 18th birthday falls on October 3 stops being added to the award on October 2.
